entries.reason: the release ladder, walked symbol by symbol over the armv7 and armv7s caches this port holds, puts these two at 10.0.1 and the other sixty-seven names of the family at 9.0 - and one object file may not carry two releases' symbols, which is why they are the object file of their own (Accelerate/SparseProduct10.m) and the other sixty-seven are not (Accelerate/SparseBLAS9.m). The same walk is the control for that measurement: every cblas_ and LAPACK name the port imports is exported from 4.0, the oldest rung held, so the import resolves on every band this port supports
entries.effect: C = alpha * op(A) * B + C with C accumulated into, in either layout, and SPARSE_SUCCESS; SPARSE_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER for an order or a transpose the enumeration does not name, for an output stride below what the layout needs (measured: an ldc of 1 against two columns is refused), for a matrix that is not one of the port's, and for a B whose row count is not A's column count, with C untouched in every refusal
entries.source: the host's own Accelerate (macOS), which the port is held against case by case by tests/backports/host/sparseblas, which runs this port's own SparseBLAS9.m and the host's library over the same inputs and compares every status, every count and every element; the header of iOS 16.4 (System/Library/Frameworks/Accelerate.framework/Frameworks/vecLib.framework/Headers/Sparse/Types.h and BLAS.h) for the declarations and the documented contract; the release ladder for what the releases this port supports export, read from their own armv7 and arm64 caches
